title: Higher direct images for quasi-compact quasi-separated morphisms
statement:
Let $u:U\to V$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated morphism
[def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] of schemes and let $F$ be an etale abelian
sheaf on $U$. Then for every $q\geq0$ the sheaf $R^qu_*F$ of
[def-weil-pbc-direct-image] is the sheafification of the presheaf on the
small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site] of $V$

$$
 W\longmapsto H^q(W\times_VU,F|)
 \qquad(W\to V\text{ etale}),
$$

and on $\Dplus(U_{\Et})$ the derived direct image $Ru_*$ is computed in each
degree by the same description, applied to a K-injective resolution
[def-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions].

proof.text: For a sheaf $F$ choose a K-injective resolution $F[0]\to I^\bullet$; for a bounded-below complex $K$ choose a K-injective resolution $K\to I^\bullet$. Such resolutions exist and any two are chain-homotopy equivalent by [prop-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions-exist]; the formula $Ru_*K=u_*I^\bullet$ is part of the definition of the derived direct image [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], with the complexes and their cohomology interpreted in [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories] and [def-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions]. Thus $R^qu_*F$ is the $q$-th cohomology sheaf of $u_*I^\bullet$ in the degree-zero case, and the same complex computes $Ru_*K$ in every degree.

Let $W\to V$ be etale and put $j:W\times_VU\to U$. By etale base change [lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-finite-limits], $j$ is etale and the restriction of $I^\bullet$ to $W\times_VU$ is the inverse-image/restriction of $I^\bullet$. This restriction is exact on abelian sheaves by the sectionwise description of etale restriction [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-restriction] and exactness of limits and colimits of sheaves [lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-exact]. The exact left adjoint $j_!$ is the extension by zero [def-weil-pbc-etale-sum-extension], and [lem-weil-pbc-etale-restriction-injectives] gives this adjunction; hence [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective] shows that $j^{-1}I^\bullet$ is K-injective. Therefore $F|_{W\times_VU}\to j^{-1}I^\bullet$ is a K-injective resolution.

By the definition of etale cohomology [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology] and resolution independence [prop-weil-pbc-cohomology-resolution-independent], the degree-$q$ cohomology of the section complex is
$$
H^q\bigl(\Gamma(W\times_VU,j^{-1}I^\bullet)\bigr)=H^q(W\times_VU,F|).
$$
The direct-image formula [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] identifies the complex of sections of $u_*I^\bullet$ over $W$ with $I^\bullet(W\times_VU)$, and the restriction maps in $W$ are the corresponding maps of fibre products. Thus the presheaf $W\mapsto H^q((u_*I^\bullet)(W))$ is the presheaf $W\mapsto H^q(W\times_VU,F|)$ in the degree-zero case, and the same statement with hypercohomology holds for $K$.

For any complex of sheaves $C^\bullet$ on $V_{\Et}$, its underlying presheaf has sectionwise cohomology $W\mapsto H^q(C^\bullet(W))$. Sheafification is exact and commutes with this cohomology by [lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-exact] and the exact-functor cohomology lemma [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology]. Applying this to $C^\bullet=u_*I^\bullet$ gives a canonical isomorphism between the sheaf $\mathcal H^q(u_*I^\bullet)$ and the sheafification of $W\mapsto H^q((u_*I^\bullet)(W))$.

Combining the first step with the preceding two steps identifies $R^qu_*F=\mathcal H^q(Ru_*F)$ with the sheafification of $W\mapsto H^q(W\times_VU,F|)$. For $K\in\Dplus(U_{\Et})$, the first step gives $Ru_*K=u_*I^\bullet$ and the same sectionwise and sheafification calculation in every degree identifies $\mathcal H^q(Ru_*K)$ with the sheafification of $W\mapsto H^q(W\times_VU,K|)$, which is the asserted derived description.
